lane_name: H77-BGB: Buried Half-Graben Growth-Wedge Inflection x Transtensional Strain-Partitioning Gradient x Illite-Smectite Conductivity-Margin Breach
hypothesis: Blind Quaternary normal and transtensional faults in northwestern Great Basin sedimentary basins lack surface scarps where Holocene playa sedimentation or argillic hydrothermal alteration outpaces vertical slip, yet they preserve three coupled subsurface physical signatures: (1) an asymmetric cross-strike basement inflection dipole where the 2D Hessian of pre-Tertiary basement depth (depth_to_base_surf, Band 15) projected onto the unit horizontal gravity gradient normal n_g = grad(g)/|grad(g)| (from iso_grav_anom Band 13) peaks beneath flat basin floors (low det_elev_slope Band 19); (2) a spatial gradient in the dimensionless kinematic transtensional strain-partitioning index tau_ext = geod_dilaterate / sqrt(geod_dilaterate^2 + geod_shearrate^2) coupled with high geodetic 2nd invariant strain rate relative to smoothed seismic moment release (Bands 4, 7, 8, 10, 16); and (3) an illite-smectite hydrothermal upflow breach where a steep lateral gradient in log surface electrical conductivity |grad log(1 + cond_surf)| (Band 17) coincides with a shallow hydrothermal magnetite-destruction trough (upward-continued TMI_up150 exceeding shallow RTP with positive RTP Laplacian trough) and DOE GDR 1391 chemical geothermometer disequilibrium.
physical_mechanism: 10 label-free channels across 3 sub-blocks: Sub-block A projects grad(depth_to_base_surf) and Hess(depth_to_base_surf) onto the gravity horizontal gradient normal n_g = grad(g)/|grad(g)| weighted by exp(-det_elev_slope / P60); Sub-block B computes tau_ext = dil / sqrt(dil^2 + shear^2) and |grad(tau_ext)| * rank(geod_2ndinv); Sub-block C couples |grad log(1 + cond_surf)| with max(0, rank(TMI_up150) - rank(RTP)) + RTP Laplacian trough and GDR 1391 silica/cation geothermometer disequilibrium Delta_T = max(T_quartz, T_chalc, T_cat) - T_meas.
named_non_fault_mimicking_process: Buried pre-Tertiary paleochannel incised-valley fills or Mesozoic pluton/caldera intrusive margins beneath flat saline playa lakebeds, which can create basement depth curvature steps along gravity gradients, sharp lateral electrical conductivity transitions at saline/freshwater interfaces, and primary low-magnetization felsic volcanic troughs without an active Quaternary fault conduit.
